question: Does a fixed change of distance features and train-only conditioning improve correspondence-specific evidence decoding?
split: Reuse original disjoint 16 anchor/24 fit/24 evaluation histories. Fresh parameter seeds provide confirmation; binary histories are the same finite corpus.
contrast: Squared normalized anchor distances minus their within-row mean across anchors. This removes the common state-norm term and exposes signed anchor-span linear coordinates up to anchor constants.
whitening: Fit mean and covariance only on pooled training-seed fitting histories. Symmetric eigenvalue whitening retains eigenvalues >1e-8 times maximum; discarded directions map to zero. Freeze before fresh evaluation collection. Ridge alpha1, same existing train-only feature standardization.
affine_control: Fit six signed cue bits plus intercept to each seed's 16 anchor states without evaluation labels, then apply the same contrasts/whitening pipeline. Independently fit its training readout.
controls: same 32 fixed anchor permutations before frozen whitening
conventional reservoir with unchanged original settings
decision_rule: Primary contrast_white R2 >=.10 and >=.10 above latest, conditional-label shuffle and permutation q95 in >=5/6 fresh seeds at each primary delay. Overall requires all four delays. Other variants are prespecified descriptive comparisons, not alternate success routes.
fitting_boundary: Only original four training seeds and their fit24 target labels fit readouts/whitening. Fresh-seed anchors calibrate distances and label-free affine map only. No evaluation labels, histories or states fit pooled objects.
precision: Reuse original float32 precision floor. Precision-limited cells cannot pass; no cutoff tuning.
claim_boundary: External feature/readout-conditioning experiment. Success does not establish novel nonlinear computation, autonomous memory use, adaptation, causal routing or architecture superiority.
falsifier: Primary conditioned contrasts fail the declared fresh-seed criterion. Alternative variants cannot rescue it.
